entries:
Alpha 1.0.59 (a clearer adventure)

  • Keep the story in focus: Optional daily offers start collapsed beside an active Chronicle. Expand Daily contracts when you want them; ready turn-ins and accepted work appear before unaccepted offers.
  • A journal that keeps your place: Daily contracts and Recovered Lore remember their separate expanded states and keyboard focus while the journal refreshes. Phone daily summaries stack labels and rewards for easier reading.
  • Know your opponent: Target cards show the enemy's level, including in the compact phone title.
  • Honest combat information: The target card shows Attack power and the selected ability's configured mana cost, including discounts, instead of invented damage estimates. These are not promises of final damage against a target; actual combat formulas are unchanged.
  • Readable action labels: Long desktop action messages stay compact instead of stretching across the encounter. Their full text remains available to assistive technology.
  • Your progress stays yours: Town recovery and Well Rested remain intact. This interface release does not change quest requirements, rewards, leveling or drop rates; the expanded campaign and balance pass remain in development.

Alpha 1.0.58 (a reason to come home)

  • Recover in town: Living characters in Lanternhold and designated safe zones restore 10% of maximum health and mana per second. Outside safety, the 0.01 passive regeneration rate per relevant stat remains unchanged.
  • Bank your rest: Each second alive and online in a safe zone earns one second of Well Rested, up to two hours. Standing in town is enough; no sitting action is required. The duration counts down only outside safe zones.
  • Return stronger: Well Rested increases character stats by 10% and experience from enemy kills by 25%. It does not multiply gold, quest rewards or room-clear rewards. At maximum level, eligible kill XP still follows the normal Resonance conversion.
  • A little golden light: A golden elemental aura and buff timer show your rest. The effect follows graphics settings, disappears on expiry and stays hidden during stealth.
  • Rest belongs to your character: Remaining rest is saved across reconnects. Offline time neither earns nor spends rest and does not heal you. Corpses do not heal or earn rest; you still need to Respawn. Being inside a safe zone pauses rest consumption even while dead.
  • The campaign stays familiar: Existing quests, experience requirements and reward budgets are unchanged in this release. The expanded story and broader balancing pass remain separate work.
  • Safer save upgrades: Deployments retain the previous server image before building its replacement, so the required character-data backup can complete. Private recovery archives stay outside the build context.

Alpha 1.0.57 (the Chronicle remembers)

  • Your resources survive reconnects: Rejoining keeps your current character when it is still on the server. Fresh sessions restore saved health, mana and death state—including an empty mana bar—instead of granting a free refill. Offline time does not heal you.
  • One character, one owner: Replacement connections and character saves are coordinated, so an older connection cannot overwrite the new session's progress. Rejoining does not reset an active character's cooldowns.
  • Safer saves and shutdowns: Full pending character saves are journaled and recovered before login. Orderly shutdown drains accepted work and records final snapshots; abrupt failures recover the latest durable save, not every unsaved combat frame. Save-format upgrades now take a paired backup before switching servers.
  • The trading house keeps its promises: Listing deposits, bids, buyouts, refunds, sale proceeds and item deliveries have durable recovery records. Retrying a recovered operation does not charge or deliver it twice, and listings receive their full selected duration when first published.
  • List the item you selected: A changed or moved bag item now invalidates the trading-house selection. Reselect it before listing; the server verifies the exact item and stack as well.
  • Recovery rules stay explicit: Respawn restores a dead character's resources; living Recall is not a mana refill. Passive regeneration remains 0.01 per stat. Safe-zone recovery and Well Rested are planned separately and are not included in this release.

Alpha 1.0.56 (guarding the Chronicle)

  • Protecting newer saves: The server now checks the database format before startup. If a newer release has upgraded that format, this release refuses to run instead of risking your characters with an older save writer.
  • A safer recovery path: Deployment checks compatibility before replacing the running game server. An incompatible release leaves that server running and reports the problem without changing saves or database indexes. Recovery requires a compatible server; changing or deleting the database version is not a safe downgrade.
  • Clean disconnects: Joining, rejoining and closing a player's connection now synchronize character identity, snapshot history and outgoing messages with world updates, preventing connection-state races.
  • Scenery settles promptly: Dungeon-entrance cutaways now follow elapsed time, so restoring the landmark does not linger when rendering slows down. Collisions, shadows and combat timing are unchanged.
  • The same adventure today: This prepares for later persistence improvements. It does not yet change reconnect resource behavior, auction transactions, rewards or the 0.01 passive regeneration rate.

Alpha 1.0.55 (empty means empty)

  • No phantom mana refill: Spending your last mana now shows an empty bar and zero mana, instead of incorrectly displaying 100.
  • Bars that stay within bounds: Health and mana displays handle empty, missing and over-cap values without overflowing or showing invalid numbers. Normal recovery refreshes the same HUD on desktop and phone.
  • Your resources stay yours: This fixes the display only. Mana costs, health, saved progress and the 0.01 passive regeneration rate are unchanged.

Alpha 1.0.54 (know your strength)

  • Your class, your primary stat: Offline heroes and local equipment recalculations now use the same basic-attack formula as the server: Strength for Fighters, Dexterity for Rogues, Intelligence for Wizards and Wisdom for Clerics.
  • Honest weapon damage: Basic damage uses one quarter of your primary stat, rounded down, then adds flat weapon and equipment damage. The old local Strength-times-two calculation no longer inflates or misrepresents hero damage.
  • The server keeps its rules: Online damage formulas, attack speed, enemies, rewards and the 0.01 passive regeneration rate are unchanged. Your saved equipment and stat investments remain intact.

Alpha 1.0.53 (names above the crowd)

  • Names you can read: World names keep a readable screen size as you zoom or rotate your phone, instead of shrinking into tiny text above the characters.
  • Focus on who matters: Your selected target has a highlighted name. Nearby NPCs and party members take priority, while overlapping labels are hidden to keep crowds readable. The characters themselves remain visible and selectable.
  • Room for the quest marker: NPC names sit clear of their gold and blue quest markers. Moving, changing targets and switching graphics quality keep the same readable label layout.
  • The same adventure underneath: This is a presentation change. Combat, rewards, equipment, quest progress and the 0.01 passive regeneration rate are unchanged.

Alpha 1.0.52 (a second breath)

  • Recover both resources after death: Respawning in Lanternhold now restores mana as well as health, so a fallen adventurer can return to the fight with both bars ready.
  • Recovery is not a free refill: Living unstuck requests and Recall do not refill mana. Arena recovery still follows the match rules, and respawning does not reset ability cooldowns.
  • Passive regeneration stays slower: The requested 0.01 health and mana regeneration per relevant stat point per second is unchanged. This patch adds no potion or rest system.
  • Your progress stays yours: Death recovery does not change quest progress, rewards, equipment, gold or training. The current experience curve and quest catalog remain in place.

Alpha 1.0.51 (the Chronicle keeps its promises)

  • Room experience counts immediately: Clearing a dungeon room can now trigger earned levels, stat growth and unlocks immediately, using the same progression path as combat and quest rewards. Room payout amounts are unchanged.
  • Earned progress survives a return: Saved characters now identify their progression format. Previously pending levels are honored once, and the compatibility path preserves level progress when moving between supported formats without turning a full level-cap bar into unearned Resonance.
  • A promise remains a promise: Accepted quest rewards and kill requirements are retained, including explicit zero-reward offers. Saved discoveries and optional story records remain intact through catalog refreshes.
  • Your equipment stays yours: Save compatibility retains earned gear, gold, spent skill points and Forge precision. Ordinary login and save checks cover activation, rollback and reactivation across all four classes.
  • Preparation, not the balance expansion: This release keeps the current experience curve and quest catalog. The revised reward budgets, longer Chronicle and additional investigations remain in testing; the compatibility step prepares existing saves for that later change.

Alpha 1.0.50 (less clutter on the road)

  • Keep moving out of combat: Clicking clear ground after a basic attack no longer lets a delayed attack update leave your character standing still. Server-controlled Charge and death still take priority over local movement.
  • Fewer routine equipment drops: Ordinary non-boss enemies now drop equipment 40% less often. Non-boss elites retain at most one equipment piece from their loot rolls, keeping the first result rather than rerolling for a better rarity.
  • Materials keep their place: Shard and heart candidates are preserved, along with the separate material and gem rolls. Reducing equipment clutter does not secretly reduce your Forge-material supply.
  • Boss rewards stay intact: Recognized bosses keep their existing ground loot and direct rewards, including Heroic/Mythic and weekly reward rules. Party master-loot rules, personal quest fragments and full-bag protections are unchanged.
  • Keep what you have earned: Existing equipment, item stats, rarity, gold and levels are not reduced. Retained new items keep their original rolls; accepted quest requirements and rewards are unchanged.
  • More balance work ahead: This is the routine-equipment frequency pass, not final XP, quest-gold, rarity-power or endgame affordability tuning. The expanded investigation story is still in development.
